title: Customer Lift Map - Priority Grid for QBRs
content:
Purpose: lightweight, operational sheet to run during QBR prep and renewal triage. The goal is to combine 'lift potential' (expansion/opportunity) with risk signals (health/usage/contract timing) so CSMs and AMs can prioritize outreach and playbooks quickly.

How to use (quick):
- Pull latest billing/ARR + last 90d usage snapshot into the sheet.
- Populate ICP-fit (0-10), Health (0-10), Usage Trend (0-10), Deployment Complexity (0-10), Region (text), Renewal date (YYYY-MM-DD), ARR ($).
- Compute two composite scores: 
  * LiftScore = round(ICP_fit*0.4 + UsageTrend*0.25 + ExpansionSignals*0.35)  -- proxy for expansion upside
  * RiskScore = round((10-Health)*0.45 + (DeploymentComplexity)*0.25 + RenewalProximityScore*0.3) -- higher means more at risk
  where RenewalProximityScore = 10 if renewal <90 days, 7 if 90-180, 4 if 180-270, 1 otherwise.

Priority Grid (interpretation):
- Quadrant A (High Lift / High Risk): immediate outreach + executive sponsor + renewal playbook. Target: protect ARR and capture expansion while stabilizing health.
- Quadrant B (High Lift / Low Risk): strategic upsell motions, product-led campaigns, low-touch pilot offers. Cadence: standard QBR + expansion proposal.
- Quadrant C (Low Lift / High Risk): retention-first actions — technical deep-dive, SRE/solutions engineering triage, potential discount/flex terms if justified.
- Quadrant D (Low Lift / Low Risk): maintain, light-touch renewals; archive playbook, monitor usage.

Column definitions / notes:
- ICP-fit (0-10): how closely customer matches target personas (AI-native product, platform team, enterprise regulated). 10 = perfect fit.
- Health (0-10): composite of error rate, failure to complete runs, SLA breaches, support volume. 10 = excellent.
- Usage Trend (0-10): direction + momentum of token consumption relative to past quarter. 10 = strong upward trend.
- ExpansionSignals (0-10): new teams onboarding, feature requests for paid features, roadmap alignment signals.
- Deployment Complexity (0-10): 0 = simple hosted API, 10 = on-prem private with HSM and air-gapped integrations. Drives effort/cost to remediate.
- Region: NA / EMEA / APAC (affects SRE/CS coverage and SLA expectations).
- Renewal date and ARR: used for financial prioritization.

Sample rows (fill during weekly renewal triage):
- Acme Insights | ICP 9 | Health 5 | Usage 7 | Expansion 8 | Deploy 3 | Region NA | Renewal 2025-02-18 | ARR $420k -> LiftScore 8, RiskScore 7 -> Quadrant A -> Owner: SE/CS + AE; Action: schedule exec QBR + propose reserved capacity pilot.
- Nimbus Retail | ICP 6 | Health 8 | Usage 4 | Expansion 3 | Deploy 7 | Region EMEA | Renewal 2025-06-01 | ARR $95k -> LiftScore 4, RiskScore 6 -> Quadrant C -> Owner: CSM; Action: technical ops call + deployment checklist.
- BlueArc Finance | ICP 10 | Health 9 | Usage 9 | Expansion 9 | Deploy 6 | Region NA | Renewal 2026-01-12 | ARR $1.2M -> LiftScore 9, RiskScore 2 -> Quadrant B -> Owner: AE + CS; Action: strategic upsell proposal + 6-month roadmap sync.
- HarborGov Labs | ICP 4 | Health 3 | Usage 2 | Expansion 1 | Deploy 10 | Region NA | Renewal 2025-03-05 | ARR $75k -> LiftScore 1, RiskScore 9 -> Quadrant A (but low lift) -> Owner: CS escalation; Action: urgent remediation, legal review for renewal terms.
- Solace Media | ICP 7 | Health 7 | Usage 6 | Expansion 5 | Deploy 2 | Region APAC | Renewal 2025-04-20 | ARR $210k -> LiftScore 6, RiskScore 4 -> Quadrant B -> Owner: CSM; Action: standard QBR + targeted upsell.

Playbooks by quadrant (short):
- Quadrant A (High Lift/High Risk): 1) 48-hour triage, 2) exec stakeholder intro + alignment doc, 3) dedicated SE + 2-week remediation sprint, 4) renewal negotiation anchored to performance SLAs, 5) offer pilot discounted reserved capacity to fix latency/cost issues.
- Quadrant B (High Lift/Low Risk): 1) prepare expansion package (usage-based discounts, committed ARR tiers), 2) propose product roadmap tie-ins, 3) 30-60 day proof-of-value for new teams, 4) highlight cost optimizations (batching/quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize).
- Quadrant C (Low Lift/High Risk): 1) technical forensics + SRE ticket blitz, 2) evaluate cost-to-serve vs ARR, 3) consider simplified SaaS migration or sunset plan, 4) urgent QBR to get commitment on remediation timeline.
- Quadrant D (Low Lift/Low Risk): 1) renew with minimal touch, 2) product announcements mailing list, 3) 6-12 month review cadence.

Operational tips / shorthand for CSMs:
- Use 'quick wins' list when you have <30m with an executive: 1) show token-cost breakdown, 2) surface top 3 errors impacting latency, 3) request an internal champion for rollout.
- If DeployComplexity >=8, loop in Solutions Eng early; drafts of SOW take 2-3 weeks.
- Flag accounts with cross-region dependencies to GeoLead (tagged in internal slack #cs-escalations).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we replace fixed weight formula with learned weights from prior renewals? (Priya want to run A/B on last 12 months)
- Add column for 'SLA credit risk' (legal exposure) — need input from finance.
- Automate RenewalProximityScore from billing export.
- Fold in Eval/regression alerts from Redwood Optimize as an ExpansionSignal.

Appendix: suggested fields for the working sheet (copy into Google Sheet):
- Account name, Account ID, ARR, Renewal Date, ICP_fit (0-10), Health (0-10), UsageTrend (0-10), ExpansionSignals (0-10), DeploymentComplexity (0-10), Region, Current tier (PLG/SMB/Enterprise), Owner (CS/AE), Last contact date, Next steps, QBR_priority (A/B/C/D label), Notes.

Slack refs and tickets to link during prep: 
- #cs-qbr-prep (template messages), #cs-escalations (severe issues), JIRA CS tickets created for remediation (prefix CS-T).

Versioning: this is a working draft — expect changes after two quarters of use. Keep a changelog entry in Confluence: CONFLUENCE-CSR-PRIORITY-RUBRIC.

End of doc.
